messages.author: ad331caa97d1c9b0
messages.subject: TSKYC in metout and shadmet
parts:
Hi Mike/All,

I was plotting "TSKYC: sky radiant temperature" under zero shade and 90% shade (see following figure), generated by micro_era5 for July in 1999 at a desert site (E39.077, N25.602). I found the TSKYC under 90% shade are much higher than those under zero shade. Does this reflect a canopy effect? When I run endo_R for an individual under zero shade and 90% shade respectively, should I use these two different sets of TSKYC for the endo_R parameter "TSKY", respectively?

Your help would be most appreciated!

All the best,

Liang

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: TSKYC in metout and shadmet
parts:
Hi Liang,

Yes TSKYC accounts for effects of cloud and shade and so does include the canopy effect, as well as the horizon angle effect. And yes you should definitely use two different sky temperatures for zero and 90% shade. It makes quite a big difference.

All the best,
Mike
